top.line: The reading account, as built: the meter, credit, Stripe top-ups and the account in your own vault run today; checking payments is proposed.
top.para: An email agent told a reader none of it was built; half of that was wrong, because no page said what runs. Built: the meter, £5 of credit, Stripe top-ups, the account in the reader's vault with per-device files, a consolidated balance, merged devices, notes and a lane. Proposed: payments checked against Stripe and signed.

in-short.line: Seven lines: the meter and top-ups, the vault account, a balance across devices, the lane, ciphertext, the check, this page.
in-short.para: The meter, credit and Stripe top-ups run. The account sits in the reader's vault, one file per device. The balance is consolidated, a payment counted once. Any browser can write to the vault's lane. The server sees ciphertext. Checking and signing payments is proposed. This page says what is built.

why.line: Why this page: an email agent read our articles and called the reader's vault account a proposal.
why.para: Half of its sentence was wrong: the meter and the credit kept in the reader's vault are built, and used daily; only validated, signed payments are proposed. The billing article said the credit was kept in the browser, and no page listed what runs. That documentation gap is ours, and this page and a corrected billing article fill it.

built.line: What is built: the meter, starting credit, Stripe top-ups, the vault account, a consolidated balance, merged devices, notes and the lane.
built.para: Pages charge by how much was read; £5 starting credit per account; a £5 payment link since 11 October, credited once per payment reference; per-device files of raw records in a passkey-opened vault; balances computed across devices; duplicates merged; notes; a lane any browser can write to; a server that sees only ciphertext.

mine.line: What it looks like from here: £2 left, every device and every page in my vault, records from the lane.
mine.para: I use it every day and am about to top up. My vault shows each device I read on and the pages opened on each, and records from a browser without the passkey arrived through the lane. With no server keeping the balance, it is quite powerful, and the base the billing design builds on.

proposed.line: What is proposed: payments checked against Stripe, signed validations, and one account across our sites.
proposed.para: The return page says it adds the top-up and cannot verify the payment. The proposal reconciles each payment with Stripe later, signs the result into a vault both sides write to, so credit is unvalidated, validated or not valid, and moves the account to user.sgit.ai or billing.sgit.ai for every site.

limits.line: As of this release; top-ups are not verified; the vault is optional; the email agent's draft paraphrased.
limits.para: Checked against the code and tests of 21 October 2026. The return page trusts the payment reference, the gap the proposal closes. Without a passkey the account stays in the browser. The draft is paraphrased to correct it, not to blame it.

sources.line: The account's code, the Stripe return page, this release's tests, my own account, and related articles.
sources.para: The meter, the browser-to-vault sync, the vault pane and lane, the page Stripe returns to and the release's test logs, read on 21 October 2026; my own account; a draft from the email agent, paraphrased; and the user keeps the meter, paying after the value, the vault opened, and sixteen notes.
